Okay so alien fire team elite is a great game that I was greatly surprised by. The story is nothing special and it's not really scary at all. However this game is just such a good shooter. I don't love 3rd person shooters, or games at all but this one really works for me. The combat is fast paced and the environment looks very alien like. Seeing a swarm of xenos coming at you is epic.
Runs well too, 90FPS or 45-60 on steam deck with maxed settings, steam deck at 50 percent res.
Overall it's not what I expected and it is not near as scary as I had hoped it would be but I do love this game. For the price I paid, only 6 pounds it's an easy 10/10 would recommend.

[b]Aliens: Fireteam Elite - Into the Hive Edition[/b] is a solid cooperative shooter that captures the military action and industrial tension of James Cameron's [i]Aliens[/i].

The PC version is significantly improved from the launch experience I had on Xbox Series X, and the [i]Pathogen[/i] expansion gives the campaign a much stronger finish.

[h2]The Good[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Atmosphere[/b]: Industrial environments, Xenomorph pressure, and Colonial Marine presentation make it feel authentically tied to [i]Aliens[/i].
[*][b]Combat[/b]: Swarming enemies make positioning, resource management, and teamwork consistently important.
[*][b]Class Design[/b]: Seven distinct kits, perks, weapons, and attachments support meaningful fireteam roles and loadout experimentation.
[*][b]Pathogen[/b]: New enemies, weapons, missions, and a memorable finale improve on the base campaign.
[/list]

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Mission Variety[/b]: Repeated objectives and linear mission structure limit long-term replayability.
[*][b]Solo Play[/b]: Alpha and Beta become much less dependable once encounters demand tighter coordination.
[/list]

[h2]Summary[/h2]
[b]Aliens: Fireteam Elite - Into the Hive Edition[/b] works best when played as an actual fireteam.

The class system, weapon customization, and constant Xenomorph pressure create satisfying cooperative encounters where positioning and communication matter more than simply holding the trigger.

Its biggest weakness is repetition. The same mission structure eventually becomes predictable, and AI teammates cannot replace human coordination on harder content.

The [i]Pathogen[/i] expansion helps considerably, delivering stronger encounters and the campaign's best finale.

It never reaches the top tier of cooperative shooters, but for fans of [i]Aliens[/i] looking for a good bug hunt with friends, it delivers.

[b]Score: 6.5 / 10[/b]
[b]Recommended[/b]
